scope.summary: Harden the spawned-process reclaim reaper beyond the MT-007 crash->restart boot case: cover the running-app window and decide fail-open vs fail-closed on kill failure. MT-007's blocker (generic reclaim wired into boot) is closed and runtime-proven; these are secondary residuals surfaced by adversarial review, deferred so they are not forgotten.
scope.root_cause: The boot reclaimer only surfaces dead-prior-owner (crash->restart) orphans; the periodic staleness task restart pass is disabled post-boot, and its stale_sessions query vetoes rows lacking a model_lanes record, so a live-instance official-CLI (no-lane) orphan is reaped only at the NEXT boot.
forbidden_paths: weakening the pid + creation-time + exe-sha256 process identity fence
fabricating a STOP from unproven kill evidence
acceptance_criteria: F1 (MAJOR): a same-instance mid-run official-CLI (no model_lanes row) orphan whose process terminated/reap-failed is reaped by the RUNNING app (staleness task or a CLI-session-end reclaim trigger), not only at next boot; add a runtime proof.

F2 (MAJOR): decide+implement the intended post-boot staleness restart-pass semantics (currently run_restart_pass=false) so restart-orphans get periodic re-surfacing if the boot pass is skipped/times out, OR document why boot-only suffices.

F3 (design decision, operator): kill-failure at boot is currently fail-OPEN (row left OPEN, boot continues). Decide resilient-boot (fail-open + retry) vs hard fail-closed (boot Err on un-reapable orphan); implement+prove the chosen contract incl. the non-Windows unavailable-adapter path (KillOutcome::Failed + row stays open).

F4 (MINOR): HANDSHAKE_STARTUP_RECOVERY_ONLY=1 returns before production_with_lease so it never surfaces generic spawned-process orphans; run reconcile_restart_orphans_at_boot in that branch too, or document the exclusion.

F5 (MINOR): reclaim.rs docstring/comment overstate fail-closed (true only for store/surfacing errors); RestartOrphanBootReconcileReport.processes_reclaimed counts KillOutcome::Failed as reclaimed. Correct the doc and count only Killed|KilledPendingStop (add processes_kill_failed).

F6 (MINOR): fold the staleness task inline restart loop (reclaim.rs ~4314) into reconcile_restart_orphans_at_boot with a caller-chosen error policy to prevent drift, OR document the intentional divergence; boot call site silently drops in-progress-reconcile sweep errors (ReclaimKillOperationSweep.reclaim_error).

F7 (NIT): MT-007 boot proof uses ProductionSandboxKill::new (default registry) and bypasses the production_with_lease 30s timeout wrapper; add coverage exercising with_registry(production_process_sandbox_registry()) + timeout. free_loopback_udp_port has an ephemeral-port re-bind flake window; retry or skip.

P-1 (PREREQUISITE, before F1/F2): stale_sessions no longer panics on a NULL parent_session_id row; the row class is filtered in SQL and decoded with try_get; a PG regression test proves stale_sessions returns Ok for an adapter-owned self-owned NULL-parent_session_id open row; a panicking scan can no longer silently disable the periodic reclaim task.

P-2 (PREREQUISITE, before F1): the running-app reap can actually claim the target rows - either parent_session_id is populated for auth-status/preflight/login CLI children, or a claim-by-process_uuid path exists. The F1 proof asserts the exact process_uuid appears in processes_reclaimed with KillOutcome::Killed, never merely is_ok().

P-3 (PREREQUISITE, before F1): PostgresProcessLedgerStore overrides active_process_for_session with a single-row claim, and a PG test proves a sibling row's reclaim_claim metadata is unchanged across a run_process targeting a different process_uuid in the same session.

P-4 (PREREQUISITE, before F2): the periodic restart pass cannot kill a live instance's healthy children - the UDP lease is not released before process exit (or only after proving zero open rows), the dead-owner probe requires two samples at least one scan interval apart, and the claim path carries an explicit owner_runtime_instance_id predicate.

P-5: the reclaim hook is invoked only from record_stop's two branches and the terminate_and_collect reap failure, never from Drop; it runs after the STOP permit is released, via the wait_stop_durability_blocking thread + current_thread-runtime pattern, under an explicit timeout well below 30s, and guards lifecycle.is_none().

P-6 (PROOF HONESTY, applies to every proof command in this MT): each --exact proof asserts a non-zero executed-test count or greps --nocapture output for the test name, because cargo exits 0 when an --exact filter matches nothing.
scope.risk_if_missed: A live-app official-CLI orphan can stay OPEN until the next restart; an un-reapable orphan is silently left open with an overstated fail-closed claim.

implementation_notes: F1: reap at the hook, not by relaxing stale_sessions. Give GuardedCliChild an Option<Arc<Reclaim>> and call run_process(parent_session_id, process_uuid, ReclaimTrigger::Failure) from official_cli_bridge.rs leave_open_for_reconciliation. run_process uses active_process_for_session and bypasses the session-wide veto in stale_sessions. Existing in-repo precedent: api/palmistry.rs survivor cleanup and coordinator.rs teardown failure both already call run_process this way.

F1 DO NOT relax reclaim.rs stale_sessions None=>false to true: the row carries no liveness evidence and is owned by the LIVE instance, so that would kill healthy in-flight official-CLI children. A negative test must prove a live same-instance child is never killed.

F2: on the real boot path spawn_managed_staleness_reclaim_task_after_boot passes run_restart_pass=false, so restart_sessions runs exactly once inline in production_with_lease. A boot-pass TIMEOUT is already fail-closed (production_with_lease returns Err). The genuine gap is the SKIPPED case; add a periodic restart tick.

F3 OPERATOR DECISION 2026-07-30 = RESILIENT BOOT (fail-open + explicit surfacing + retry). Keep run_claimed returning Ok on KillOutcome::Failed. Make the fail-open explicit: count kill-failures separately, surface them out of boot (runtime.rs currently discards the whole report), and retry via F2. Do NOT make boot return Err: the native reclaim adapter is Windows-only and always returns Failed off-Windows, which would permanently brick boot; and fail-closed cannot distinguish a correct refusal-to-kill (pid-reuse guard) from a genuine reap failure.

F4: HANDSHAKE_STARTUP_RECOVERY_ONLY=1 returns in main.rs ~271 before production_with_lease (~447), so reconcile_restart_orphans_at_boot never runs and only reclaim_pidless_embedded_orphans executes. Any added pass must complete BEFORE managed_pg.stop() in that branch.

F5: reclaim.rs processes_reclaimed uses .len() over all ReclaimedProcess, counting Failed as reclaimed. Count only Killed|KilledPendingStop and add processes_kill_failed. The report has ZERO existing read sites (runtime.rs discards it), and derive(Default) means adding a field needs no other construction edit. Discrimination reference impl already exists in mt_executor/cancellation.rs TryFrom<ReclaimReport>.

F5: correct the doc overstatements - reclaim.rs RestartOrphanBootReconcileReport doc says fenced-closed (not a KillOutcome variant) and claims fail-closed error semantics; runtime.rs claims it reclaims every generic spawned-process orphan. Neither is true for kill failure.

F6: fold the staleness inline restart loop into reconcile_restart_orphans_at_boot with a caller-chosen error policy (abort vs log-and-continue) plus a cancellation hook - the same seam F3 needs. Also stop dropping ReclaimKillOperationSweep.reclaim_error at the boot call site.

F7: the MT-007 boot proof uses ProductionSandboxKill::new (default registry, HandshakeNative only) and calls reconcile_restart_orphans_at_boot directly, bypassing production_with_lease and its 30s timeout. production_process_sandbox_registry() and with_registry have ZERO occurrences under tests/. Add coverage using the production registry plus the timeout wrapper. Also retry free_loopback_udp_port: the drop-then-probe window lets another host process take the ephemeral port and silently veto surfacing.

HBR-MAN-004 landing spot: user_manual/seed.rs section(recovery, Hard-crash orphan reconcile) currently says nothing about restart_sessions, reconcile_restart_orphans_at_boot, the fail-open kill-failure contract, or the recovery-only exclusion. The behavior-coverage gate assertions are contains-based, so added text is safe.
NO MIGRATION REQUIRED: processes_kill_failed is an in-memory struct field; nothing in F1-F7 changes a table.

operator_decisions.question: When boot cannot reap a spawned-process orphan (kill fails), should boot fail open or fail closed?
operator_decisions.rationale: The Failed path is already truthful and idempotently retryable (claim released, fence cleared, no false STOP). Fail-closed would permanently brick boot off-Windows because the native reclaim adapter is Windows-only and always returns Failed, and it cannot distinguish a correct refusal-to-kill from a genuine reap failure.

blocking_findings.title: stale_sessions panics on NULL parent_session_id and permanently kills the staleness task
blocking_findings.detail: reclaim.rs:4065 decodes parent_session_id with the panicking accessor row.get::<String>, and the query at reclaim.rs:4040-4043 has no IS NOT NULL filter. The column is nullable (migration 0021_kernel_process_lifecycle.sql:8). A real production path writes exactly such a row: access_config.rs:389-408 (auth_status_invocation) sets session_id but never parent_session_id, while still carrying sandbox_adapter_id and the live owner_runtime_instance_id. Opening Settings spawns that CLI child; the 30s staleness tick then hits UnexpectedNullError inside the tokio::spawn task (reclaim.rs:4312) and the periodic reclaim task is silently dead for the rest of the process lifetime. If the row stays open, every subsequent boot re-arms the panic.
blocking_findings.why_it_blocks: F1's target row class (official-CLI orphan with no model_lanes record) IS the NULL-parent_session_id class, and F2's deliverable is a periodic tick on the very task that dies. The feature would be dead on arrival in the exact case it exists for.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Change reclaim.rs:4065 to try_get::<Option<String>,_> and skip/log NULL rows; add AND lifecycle.parent_session_id IS NOT NULL to reclaim.rs:4040; add a PG regression test seeding an adapter-owned, self-owned, NULL-parent_session_id open row asserting stale_sessions returns Ok instead of panicking; add supervisor logging or task restart so a panicking scan cannot silently disable reclaim.

blocking_findings.title: run_process claims by parent_session_id, which is None for exactly the rows F1 targets
blocking_findings.detail: run_process filters WHERE parent_session_id = $1 (reclaim.rs:2790, SQL at reclaim.rs:49). For swarm lanes parent_session_id is the shared coordinator session (production_factory.rs:1794-1806); for auth-status/preflight CLI children it is None (access_config.rs:389-408). Passing None or an empty string matches zero rows, so run_process returns an empty report and the test goes green while nothing was reclaimed. Those rows are also invisible to restart_sessions, which requires parent_session_id IS NOT NULL (reclaim.rs:3945-3946), so they are not reaped at next boot either.
blocking_findings.why_it_blocks: F1's acceptance criterion cannot be met, and the natural test (assert is_ok) would be a false green.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Either populate parent_session_id in the auth-status/preflight/login contexts, or add a store method that claims by process_uuid alone. The F1 proof MUST assert report.processes_reclaimed contains the exact process_uuid with KillOutcome::Killed - never merely is_ok().

blocking_findings.title: run_process mass-claims every sibling row of the parent session and can corrupt a concurrent reclaim
blocking_findings.detail: PostgresProcessLedgerStore does not override active_process_for_session; the default at reclaim.rs:2405 claims the WHOLE session set (reclaim.rs:2410) and then releases non-targets (reclaim.rs:2416-2423), skipping any sibling in kill_succeeded_pending_stop. The claim SQL re-claims those unconditionally and bumps generation (reclaim.rs:52, :82-86), so a concurrent reclaimer's generation/claimant/kill_operation match fails (reclaim.rs:3634-3639) and its clean Killed degrades to KilledPendingStop. Separately, the transient session-wide claim makes a concurrent teardown or boot pass skip those rows as claimed-with-live-lease (reclaim.rs:56-62), silently missing orphans.
blocking_findings.why_it_blocks: Today run_process is called only on rare failure paths; F1 puts it on EVERY CLI teardown that cannot prove a STOP, turning a rare race into a routine one.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Implement the single-row override the trait doc at reclaim.rs:2400-2404 already anticipates for PostgresProcessLedgerStore (WHERE process_uuid = $1 AND parent_session_id = $2) BEFORE wiring F1. Add a PG test asserting a sibling row's reclaim_claim metadata is byte-identical across a run_process on a different process_uuid in the same session.

blocking_findings.title: F2's periodic restart pass can kill another live Handshake instance's healthy children
blocking_findings.detail: restart_sessions infers 'prior owner is dead' by binding its ephemeral loopback UDP port (reclaim.rs:3993-4016, try_claim_udp_lease at :405-425). That lease is released while the host process is still alive, at runtime.rs:172-177 (shutdown_and_drain) and runtime.rs:199-201 (Drop). The Tauri shell builds its own ProcessReclaimRuntime (app/src-tauri/src/commands/swarm_runtime.rs:494) and calls shutdown_and_drain (:1209) while continuing to run with live official-CLI children and open rows. The backend's restart pass then probes the freed port, concludes the owner is dead, and kills those live healthy children. The identity fence gives NO protection: it proves the right process generation, not liveness or ownership, so it matches perfectly and the kill proceeds.
blocking_findings.why_it_blocks: Boot-only reclaim hits this window at most once per boot. A 30s periodic tick hits it roughly 2880 times per day. The Operator runs parallel Handshake sessions, so this is a live exposure, not a theoretical one.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Do not release the UDP lease before process exit (or release only after proving zero open rows for the instance); require the dead-owner probe to observe the port free across two samples separated by at least one scan interval; and add an explicit owner_runtime_instance_id != self predicate inside the claim SQL, which today has no owner filter at all (reclaim.rs:49-63) - the veto lives only in restart_sessions, so any future caller of Reclaim::run bypasses it.

blocking_findings.title: The Drop path cannot safely call an async reclaim; hook record_stop and terminate_and_collect only
blocking_findings.detail: leave_open_for_reconciliation is a sync fn (official_cli_bridge.rs:2256). Handle::current().block_on from Drop during unwind is a double panic -> abort; futures::executor::block_on on a tokio worker stalls it and panics without a runtime context, and Reclaim needs a real runtime (tokio::spawn reclaim.rs:3113, interval/sleep :3097/:3107, spawn_blocking handshake_native.rs:472). The only safe in-file precedent is wait_stop_durability_blocking (official_cli_bridge.rs:1594-1620): thread::spawn + current_thread runtime + block_on + join, mapping join panic to an error. Cost is real: RECLAIM_KILL_TIMEOUT is 30s (reclaim.rs:2086) plus a 5s stop-ack, and auth_status is a sync trait method (access_config.rs:310-340) whose axum caller would block a worker ~35s.
blocking_findings.why_it_blocks: A naive implementation aborts the process or stalls the runtime. Also an ordering hazard: if the reclaim is called before lifecycle.leave_open_for_reconciliation() at :2261, the guard still holds its STOP permit and run_claimed aborts at reclaim.rs:2808-2818 on a saturated writer, reclaiming nothing.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Call reclaim only AFTER the permit is released; use the wait_stop_durability_blocking thread + current_thread-runtime pattern; apply an explicit timeout well under 30s; and do NOT hook Drop (:2320, :2325) - hook only record_stop's two branches (:2240, :2251) and the terminate_and_collect reap failure (:2282), leaving Drop cases to the periodic pass. Guard lifecycle.is_none(): the :2320 branch is reachable only when no START row exists (early return :2227-2229), so there is no process_uuid to reclaim.

additional_findings: STOP truthfulness race: on the DurabilityUnconfirmed branch the true STOP with the real exit code may still commit later (writer.rs:501-504) while a reclaim writes exit_code -1 / stop_reason 'reclaim' (reclaim.rs:2296-2328). Decide which STOP wins and test the late-commit interleaving.

ForegroundChildOwner (official_cli_bridge.rs:1663-1792) has its own leave_open_for_reconciliation at :1702 reached with the child possibly still alive, and its Drop deliberately mem::forgets child + lifecycle while the process may be live (:1780-1789). F1 does not touch it, so the login path keeps producing open rows for LIVE processes - precisely what P-4 can then kill. Declare it an explicit non-goal or cover it.

HBR-QUIET-003 gap: ownership metadata is preserved into the STOP (reclaim.rs:2331-2336) but there is NO ownership predicate anywhere in the kill path. Add owner_runtime_instance_id = self on the running-app hook's claim path so the in-app reaper structurally cannot touch another instance's process.

F5 surfacing caveat: production_with_lease's return shape is consumed by two composition roots (main.rs:447 and app/src-tauri/src/commands/swarm_runtime.rs:494); the Tauri path is under forbidden_paths. Prefer tracing::warn! plus a field on ProcessReclaimRuntime read by an existing backend surface over changing the return shape. Also model_manual/content.rs:566-572 documents processes_reclaimed but is not in allowed_paths.
